pr_title: network: DHCPv4 (client/server)- Implement IPv6 only preferred option…
pr_body:
…, RFC 8925

Implements https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8925

RFC8925 specifies a DHCPv4 option to indicate that a host supports an IPv6-only mode and is willing to forgo obtaining an IPv4 address if the network provides IPv6 connectivity. The option v6-only-preferred content is a 32-bit unsigned integer and specifies for how long the device should disable its stack. The value is expressed in seconds.


closes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/24624

issue_context.title: Please support RFC 8925 IPv6-Only Preferred Option for DHCPv4 (Option 108)
issue_context.body:
### Component

systemd-networkd

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe


Testing with systemd v251 (the latest), systemd does not follow the behavour of RFC 8925, where as MacOS v12 & iOS v15 do. Systemd still requests an IPv4 address, even though option 108 is present in the DHCP offer.


### Describe the solution you'd like

Since Oct 2020, there has been a standard for DHCPv4 clients to accept Option 108  (IPv6-Only Preferred Option), and not request an IPv4 address if the option is present. RFC 8925 specifies the client behavour: https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc8925.html

Please include DHCPv4 Option 108 in your development roadmap.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

There are few alternatives, since systemd is included in all the major Linux distros.

### The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for

_No response_
comments: This were fixed in PR #29472, thank you!

review_comments: Please use the timestamp of the lease (or maybe the timestamp of the sending request?).

The lease is irrelevant here. It's not considered as ipv6 mode is set. As per starting time, it could be a TMO in DHCP client requests and it's not constant.  The right way is to do when the offer is received and we know it's ipv6 mode only then we delay from there.
`_preferred` is an option name, and corresponds to the timespan, not a timer. Please name `timeout_ipv6_only_wait` or so, as RFC call the timer `V6ONLY_WAIT`.

From the RFC
> The server MUST NOT include the IPv6-Only Preferred option in the DHCPOFFER or DHCPACK message if the option was not present in the Parameter Request List sent by the client.

Please do not append the option unconditionally.
ohh yes . I added the condition now.

No no, in this stage, the client already sent REQUEST and received ACK.
The RFC states that the client should start the `V6ONLY_WAIT` timer when received OFFER, and the client should not send REQUEST in that case.
https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8925#name-dhcpv4-client-behavior
> If the client includes the IPv6-Only Preferred option code in the Parameter Request List and the DHCPOFFER message from the server contains a valid IPv6-Only Preferred option, the client SHOULD NOT request the IPv4 address provided in the DHCPOFFER. If the IPv6-Only Preferred option returned by the server contains a value greater than or equal to MIN_V6ONLY_WAIT, the client SHOULD set the V6ONLY_WAIT timer to that value. Otherwise, the client SHOULD set the V6ONLY_WAIT timer to MIN_V6ONLY_WAIT. The client SHOULD stop the DHCPv4 configuration process for V6ONLY_WAIT seconds or until a network attachment event, whichever happens first.

This comes in after getting the OFFER from server . ```client_handle_offer``` . We not proceeding to request

1. Discover: 
2. Offer: <HERE we are calling after receiving the offer> 
3.  Request:

Ah, indeed. Sorry. I forgot that the handler is also called after OFFER.

But, still that should not be handled here, but in sd-dhcp-client.c.
There is nothing we need to change in this handler.
Only we need to do in networkd side is stopping the DHCPv4 client when NDisc or DHCPv6 configures an IPv6 address.
The flag ```dhcp_allow_ipv6_only_mode``` which we get from user. On basic of that this operation happens. It's similar to we filter the black/white listed dhcp servers.

The RFC said,
> If the client did not include the IPv6-Only Preferred option code in the Parameter Request List in the DHCPDISCOVER or DHCPREQUEST message, it MUST ignore the IPv6-Only Preferred option in any messages received from the server.

So, the option should be ignored if the IPv6 only mode is disabled.
Correct but here we only parsing them and storing. Not using like other parameters.
